logline: A former gangster turned street-fighting lawyer teams up with a principled attorney to dismantle the corrupt judge who destroyed both their lives in the fictional port city of Kisung.

renewal.note: 16-episode single-season run completed July 2018. No renewal announced. Finale rated 8.937% on AGB Nielsen, one of the highest cable finale ratings of 2018.

bollymeter.basis: IMDb rates it 7.6/10. The finale was one of cable television's highest-rated episodes of 2018 at 8.937% (AGB Nielsen). Critics praised Lee Joon-gi's physical charisma and the villain work, while noting script inconsistency in the second half.

seasons.review_body: Lawless Lawyer premiered on tvN in May 2018 and drew strong cable ratings throughout its run, with the finale hitting 8.937% on AGB Nielsen - among the highest for a Korean cable drama that year. The show is built around Lee Joon-gi's physicality: the action choreography is kinetic and the lead's commitment to the brawling lawyer persona never wavers. Seo Yea-ji holds her own as the ethically grounded counterpart, and the antagonist duo of Choi Min-soo and Lee Hye-young deliver genuinely menacing work. The general consensus places the first eight episodes as a tight revenge thriller, with the back half becoming narratively hazier. Viewers who tune in for the action and villain dynamics will find the ride satisfying; those seeking tighter plotting in the second half may find it uneven.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: A kinetic opening that makes no apology for its pulp ambitions - the courtroom fistfight within the first ten minutes sets the show's register and Lee Joon-gi's charisma does the rest.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The moment Bong Sang-pil defends a client by threatening the opposing lawyer with physical consequences is both ridiculous and completely committed - the show's contract with the audience in one scene.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 16
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale delivers the revenge payoff viewers tuned in for, even if the path to get there required some narrative shortcuts. A satisfying close to a series that prioritised momentum over rigour.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The final confrontation in the courthouse closes the personal arc that opened the series, landing with the genre satisfaction the show promised from episode one.
